youtube_title: City West: the lost 1836 town in the Indiana Dunes that meant to rival Chicago
youtube:
It was meant to rival Chicago. In 1836, promoters started City West at the mouth of Fort Creek, in the dunes west of Michigan City. It had a sawmill, a store and a big hotel, and even Daniel Webster stopped there. Then came the Panic of 1837, and the harbor money it was counting on never came. Within a few years the town was empty. Years later, one of its buildings was hauled off to Chesterton and became a hotel, and a fire swept through and burned what was left of City West. Today the spot is part of Indiana Dunes State Park, near the beach, and nothing of the town is left. Comment your town, and it could be next! #CityWest #IndianaDunes #PorterCounty #Chesterton #GhostTown #History #LaPorteAfterDark #Shorts

All pictures are drawn; no picture of City West is known, so its buildings are drawn generic. Narration is a computer voice. Sources: T. H. Ball, Northwestern Indiana from 1800 to 1900 (1900); John O. Bowers, Dream Cities of the Calumet (1929), quoting the Chesterton Tribune (1908); Hubert Skinner, Complete History of Porter County (1878); Goodspeed & Blanchard, Counties of Porter and Lake (1882); Cannon, Loring and Robb, History of the Lake and Calumet Region (1927); The Vidette-Messenger, Porter County Centennial edition (Aug. 18, 1936); Steven R. Shook, Historical Images of Porter County; Encyclopedia of Chicago. The sources disagree on how many houses and hotels it had and on the year it burned, so this gives neither. More local history: https://laporteweathernow.com/history

factcheck: Blind independent check Nov. 16, 2026 (given only the script, on-screen text and pictures, per the playbook): 9 fixes, all made: 'speculators' became 'promoters'; the pier came out of the narration and pictures (Skinner: built 'some years after' the town was destroyed); 'a hotel' became 'a store and a big hotel'; the stagecoach came out (Ball: a two-horse carriage; the Vidette: a stagecoach); 'its hotel was hauled off' became 'one of its buildings was hauled off to Chesterton and became a hotel'; the 1854 smell and glow came out (not in Skinner; Wikipedia's line has no footnote; Bowers says no one saw the fire), and so did the fire's year and cause; the watching cabin came out; credits name the old histories, not Wikipedia.
